prompt.adult: When Jesus walked by the Sea of Galilee, what were Simon and Andrew doing?
prompt.child: Jesus walked by the Sea of Galilee and saw two brothers, Simon and Andrew. What were they doing?
prompt.teen: Walking by the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw Simon and Andrew. What were they doing?
prompt.older: According to Mark 1:16, what were Simon and Andrew doing when Jesus saw them by the Sea of Galilee?

verses.text: And as He walked by the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

explanation.adult: Mark 1:16 tells what the two brothers were doing and explains why. Read the middle of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Mark 1:16. It tells what Simon and Andrew were doing in the sea, and then says what their job was.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 1:16. It describes what the brothers were doing before it gives their job.
explanation.older: Mark 1:16 describes the brothers' activity in the sea and then gives their occupation.

teaching.extended_explanation: Mark 1:16 says the brothers were fishermen. The verse shows them at work in the sea when Jesus came by.
teaching.takeaway: Simon and Andrew were casting a net into the sea.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: What did Simon and Andrew do right after Jesus called them to come with Him?
prompt.child: Jesus called Simon and Andrew to come with Him. What did they do right away?
prompt.teen: Right after Jesus called Simon and Andrew, what did they do?
prompt.older: According to Mark 1:18, what did Simon and Andrew do immediately after Jesus called them?

verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Follow Me, and I will make you become fishers of men.”
They immediately left their nets and followed Him.

explanation.adult: Mark 1:18 tells what the brothers did as soon as Jesus called them. Read what they put down.
explanation.child: Read Mark 1:18. It tells what Simon and Andrew did right away. Look at what they set down.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 1:18. Notice the word "immediately" and what they did next.
explanation.older: Mark 1:18 records the brothers' immediate response, beginning with what they set aside.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus called in Mark 1:17, and in the very next verse the brothers acted right away. Read what they did first and then whom they followed.
teaching.takeaway: Simon and Andrew immediately left their nets and followed Jesus.

prompt.adult: James and John were mending nets in a boat. Who was their father?
prompt.child: Jesus saw two brothers, James and John, fixing nets in a boat. Who was their dad?
prompt.teen: James and John were fixing their nets in a boat. Who was their father?
prompt.older: According to Mark 1:19, whose sons were James and John, who were mending nets in their boat?

verses.text: When He had gone a little farther from there, He saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the boat mending their nets.

explanation.adult: Mark 1:19 tells whose son James was. Read the words after "James the son of."
explanation.child: Read Mark 1:19. It says "James the son of" someone. The next word is the father's name.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 1:19. The father's name comes right after "James the son of."
explanation.older: Mark 1:19 identifies James by his father's name, given right after "the son of."

teaching.extended_explanation: Mark 1:19 names James by his father, and the next verse names the same father again, left in the boat with the hired servants.
teaching.takeaway: James and John were the sons of Zebedee.

prompt.adult: On the mountain, how many men did Jesus appoint to be with Him?
prompt.child: Jesus went up on a mountain and chose some men to be with Him. How many did He choose?
prompt.teen: Jesus went up a mountain and appointed some men to be with Him. How many?
prompt.older: According to Mark 3:14, how many did Jesus appoint to be with Him?

explanation.adult: Mark 3:14 gives the number Jesus appointed. Read the words after "He appointed."
explanation.child: Read Mark 3:14. Right after "He appointed," the verse gives a number.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 3:14. The number comes right after "He appointed."
explanation.older: Mark 3:14 states the number immediately after "He appointed."

teaching.extended_explanation: Mark 3:14 gives the number, and Mark 3:16-19 then lists each man by name. You can count them to check.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus appointed twelve to be with Him.

prompt.teen: Jesus gave Simon another name. What was it?
prompt.older: According to Mark 3:16, what name did Jesus give to Simon?

verses.text: Simon, to whom He gave the name Peter;

explanation.adult: Mark 3:16 tells the name Jesus gave Simon. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Mark 3:16. The last word is the new name.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 3:16. The new name is the last word in the verse.
explanation.older: Mark 3:16 ends with the name Jesus gave to Simon.

teaching.extended_explanation: Mark 3:16 is short. It names Simon first, then tells the name Jesus gave him.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus gave Simon the name Peter.

prompt.adult: Jesus chose His closest followers to be with Him. What would He send them out to do?
prompt.child: Jesus chose some men to be with Him. What would He send them out to do?
prompt.teen: Jesus chose some followers to be with Him. What would He send them out to do?
prompt.older: According to Mark 3:14, besides being with Him, what would Jesus send them out to do?

verses.text: that He might send them out to preach,

explanation.adult: Mark 3:14 gives two reasons for choosing them. Read the end of the verse for the second.
explanation.child: Read Mark 3:14. It says they would be with Jesus and He would send them out. Read what they would do.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 3:14. After "send them out," the verse tells what they would do.
explanation.older: Mark 3:14 states the purpose of sending them out at the close of the verse.

teaching.extended_explanation: Mark 3:14 gives the first reason (to be with Jesus) and then tells the work He would send them out to do.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus would send them out to preach.

prompt.adult: Simon told Jesus they had worked hard all night. What had they caught?
prompt.child: Simon and his partners fished all night long. How many fish did they catch?
prompt.teen: Simon said they had worked all night. How many fish had they caught?
prompt.older: According to Luke 5:5, what had Simon and his partners caught after working all night?

verses.text: But Simon answered and said to Him, “Master, we have toiled all night and caught nothing; nevertheless at Your word I will let down the net.”

explanation.adult: Luke 5:5 records Simon's answer to Jesus. Read what he says about the night of fishing.
explanation.child: Read Luke 5:5. Simon tells Jesus how the night of fishing went.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 5:5. Simon says how much they caught during the night.
explanation.older: Luke 5:5 gives Simon's report of the night's work before he agrees to let down the net.

teaching.extended_explanation: Simon was tired from a long night, but he still obeyed Jesus. Luke 5:5 tells how much they had caught before that.
teaching.takeaway: They had toiled all night and caught nothing.

prompt.adult: After the great catch, the partners filled both boats with fish. What did the boats begin to do?
prompt.child: So many fish were caught that both boats were full. What did the boats start to do?
prompt.teen: Both boats were filled with fish. What did the boats begin to do?
prompt.older: According to Luke 5:7, what did both boats begin to do once they were filled with fish?

verses.text: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.

explanation.adult: Luke 5:7 tells what happened to the boats because they were so full. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 5:7. The last words tell what the heavy boats began to do.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 5:7. The end of the verse tells what the full boats started to do.
explanation.older: Luke 5:7 closes by describing the result of filling both boats.

teaching.extended_explanation: The catch was so large that partners had to come help. Luke 5:7 tells what all that weight did to the boats.
teaching.takeaway: The boats were so full of fish that they began to sink.
